description: Diagnose and fix why the whole site 'feels very heavy' and 'doesn't feel smooth', then apply further polish/adaptations. Root causes (from code inspection): (1) removing the R3F/three bundle in FEAT-001 already eliminates the single largest JS/GPU cost; (2) Lenis smooth-scroll hijacks native wheel/trackpad momentum and adds a permanent rAF loop while every other scroll listener (ScrollProgress, ScrollFocusStack, HeroVideo tilt, SiteHeader condense) piggybacks on the synthetic scroll, producing a floaty, laggy feel; (3) several always-on rAF loops run concurrently (custom-cursor tick, lenis raf, scroll-focus-stack spring); (4) ScrollFocusStack calls getBoundingClientRect() per stage on scroll (layout thrash); (5) many stacked backdrop-filter blur layers + animated aurora/atmosphere/film-grain add continuous compositor/paint cost. Fix these to make scrolling feel native and light. This feature depends on FEAT-001 (three removal) being done first.
steps: SMOOTH-SCROLL (biggest smoothness lever): In src/components/motion/smooth-scroll.tsx, make Lenis feel native rather than floaty. Reduce perceived lag by lowering `duration` from 1.05 toward ~0.8 and setting `lerp`/`wheelMultiplier` conservatively, OR (preferred, and simpler/safer) gate Lenis so it only runs on fine-pointer non-touch devices and leaves native scrolling everywhere else. Touch devices already scroll natively well; Lenis on touch is a common source of 'heaviness'. Implement: only construct Lenis when `window.matchMedia('(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)').matches` is true (mirror the supportsFinePointer pattern used in magnetic.tsx/custom-cursor.tsx), in addition to the existing SSR + reduced-motion gates. Keep the single rAF loop and full teardown. Keep the route-change scrollTo(0) reset working whether or not Lenis is active. Document the reasoning in a comment.

CUSTOM CURSOR (continuous rAF): In src/components/motion/custom-cursor.tsx the ring `tick` rAF runs forever once enabled, even when the pointer is idle and off-screen. Make it self-idling: stop scheduling new frames once the ring has settled within ~0.1px of the pointer AND the cursor is not visible, and restart the loop from onMove when the pointer moves again. This removes a permanent main-thread rAF when the user is reading, not moving the mouse. Preserve all existing behavior (fine-pointer + reduced-motion gate, is-visible/is-hovering classes, teardown).

SCROLL-FOCUS-STACK (layout thrash + always-eligible spring): In src/components/scroll-focus-stack.tsx, measure() calls getBoundingClientRect() for every stage on every scroll frame. Batch the reads so all getBoundingClientRect() calls happen together before any style writes (they already do reads-then-writes across measure/paint, but confirm no write happens between reads). More importantly, ensure the spring `paint` rAF fully stops when settled (it already returns without rescheduling when !unsettled - verify and keep). Add an IntersectionObserver or an early-out so measure() does no work (and schedules no frame) when the entire stack is scrolled out of the viewport. Keep the reduced-motion and compact-layout (max-width:900px) early-outs.

PASSIVE LISTENERS AUDIT: Confirm every scroll/touch/wheel/pointermove listener across src is registered with `{ passive: true }` where it does not call preventDefault. Files to check: scroll-progress.tsx, scroll-focus-stack.tsx, hero-video.tsx, site-shell.tsx (SiteHeader scroll + PageLayout), custom-cursor.tsx, magnetic.tsx. Fix any that are missing passive. (Note: custom-cursor's document 'pointerleave' and magnetic's node listeners can also take {passive:true}.)

REDUCE CONCURRENT COMPOSITOR COST (heaviness): In src/styles.css, reduce always-animating GPU layers that run regardless of scroll. Options, applied conservatively so the design still looks intentional: (a) ensure the animated `.site-atmosphere i`, `.aurora-blob-*`, and `.film-grain-overlay` are already neutralised under prefers-reduced-motion (they are via the guard) - keep that; (b) trim redundant stacked `backdrop-filter: blur()` where two blurred layers overlap the same region (each blur is a full-screen readback); prefer keeping blur on the header/cards but drop it where it is decorative-only and cheap to replace with a solid/gradient. Only remove blur where it does not visibly degrade the design. Do NOT remove focus-visible styles or brand tokens. Document each removal with a short comment.

WILL-CHANGE HYGIENE: In src/styles.css there are several `will-change` declarations (lines ~817, ~1240, ~1295, ~1389, ~1526-area cursor, ~2126 aurora-blob). Permanent `will-change` on many elements forces the browser to hold compositor layers indefinitely, increasing memory and paint cost = 'heavy'. Audit them: keep will-change only on elements that actually animate continuously or on hover; remove `will-change` from elements that are static most of the time (e.g. reveal targets that animate once then stop). Where an element only animates on a transient interaction, rely on the transition without a permanent will-change. Be conservative and comment the intent.

FURTHER IMPROVEMENTS / ADAPTATIONS (polish): apply low-risk, high-value refinements that make the site feel lighter and more finished, each verifiable and honest (no fabricated metrics): (a) ensure the hero <video> uses `preload="metadata"` (already set) and confirm it pauses off-screen (already implemented) - leave as-is; (b) add `content-visibility: auto` with a sensible `contain-intrinsic-size` to below-the-fold long sections (e.g. the stacked content-sections) in styles.css so off-screen sections skip rendering/layout work, reducing scroll heaviness - verify it does not break the ScrollFocusStack measurements (apply only to leaf sections that are not measured by ScrollFocusStack's getBoundingClientRect, or test that intrinsic sizing keeps layout stable); (c) confirm images/logos have width/height to avoid CLS (spot-check content-sections and showcases). Only include changes you can reason are correct-by-construction; skip anything requiring runtime measurement you cannot do in-sandbox and note it in findings.

Do NOT change site-data.ts content (site-data.test.ts pins metrics===4, projects>=16, services===4, technologies===8, industries>=15). Do NOT hand-edit src/assets/images.ts or src/routeTree.gen.ts. Keep all prefers-reduced-motion behavior and WCAG AA focus-visible styles.
acceptance_criteria: Lenis smooth-scroll no longer runs on touch/coarse-pointer devices (only constructs when hover:hover + pointer:fine, plus existing SSR + reduced-motion gates), so touch scrolling is native; desktop keeps a tightened, less-floaty smooth scroll.
custom-cursor's rAF loop stops when the ring is settled and the cursor is hidden, and resumes on pointer movement (no permanent idle rAF).
ScrollFocusStack does no per-frame work (schedules no rAF and reads no layout) while the entire stack is off-screen, and its spring rAF stops when settled.
Every scroll/touch/wheel/pointermove listener that does not preventDefault is registered { passive: true }.

Redundant overlapping backdrop-filter blur layers and unnecessary permanent will-change declarations are reduced in styles.css without removing focus-visible styles, brand tokens, or visibly degrading the design.
Below-the-fold heavy sections use content-visibility:auto with contain-intrinsic-size (or an equivalent documented optimization) without breaking ScrollFocusStack layout or reveal animations.
site-data.ts is unchanged; images.ts and routeTree.gen.ts are not hand-edited; reduced-motion and WCAG AA focus behavior preserved.
verification: Run `git grep -n "addEventListener(\"scroll\"\|addEventListener('scroll'\|pointermove\|\"wheel\"\|touchmove" src` and confirm each hit passes { passive: true } (or legitimately calls preventDefault).
Run `git grep -n "new Lenis" src` and confirm the construction is guarded by the fine-pointer check in addition to SSR + reduced-motion.
Run `git grep -n "will-change" src/styles.css` and confirm remaining occurrences are on continuously/hover-animated elements only.

Authoritative: CI (`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, node 22, npm install --legacy-peer-deps) must pass. Reason through correctness since these cannot run in-sandbox: confirm site-data.test.ts and motion.test.ts invariants are untouched, and no removed symbols are referenced.
